s: The policy of 'Security Cell' is related with
Which one of the following is not one of the objectives of Act East Policy?
o: To promote economic cooperation cultural ties and develop strategic relationship with countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
To promote peace and amity with the neighbouring countries of Asia.
To place emphasis on India ASEAN cooperation in India’s domestic agenda.
To provide enhanced connectivity to the North East of India.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Look East and Act East policies?
o: Look East was launched in the early 1990s under P.V. Narasimha Rao
Look East was originally economic, focused on trade, investment and AIFTA with ASEAN
Act East was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields
Act East was launched in 2014 at a SAARC Summit
x: Act East was launched in 2014 at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar under PM Modi, not at a SAARC Summit.

s: What is the main focus of India's Link West (Think West) policy?
o: Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific Islands
x: Link West, also called Think West, focuses on the Gulf, Iran and Israel.

s: At which forum was India's Act East Policy launched in 2014?
x: Act East was launched at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar (2014), not at a SAARC Summit.

s: Under which Prime Minister was India's Look East Policy (1991-92) launched?
x: Look East was launched under P.V. Narasimha Rao; Act East under Narendra Modi.

s: Where was India's Connect Central Asia policy launched in 2012?
x: Connect Central Asia was launched at Bishkek in 2012; Samarkand hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (2019).

s:
Consider the following statements with regard to India's Foreign Policy:

I. India's Act East Policy was originally conceived as an economic initiative but had later extended into political, strategic and cultural dimensions.

II. The 'Connect Central Asia Policy' has been taken forward with the institutionalization of the 'India-Central Asia Summit' mechanism.

III. Under the 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' (SAGAR) Policy, the DRDO initiated the Marine and Allied Interdisciplinary Training and Research Initiative (MAITRI) for the purpose of establishing long-term collaboration with countries in the East Asian region.

IV. India's Think West Policy is an outreach to the Western Industrialized nations for strengthening of relations in areas of education and defence.
Which of the above statements are valid?
x: India's Act East Policy evolved from the Look East Policy and expanded beyond economic relations into strategic and cultural engagement. The Connect Central Asia Policy is advanced through mechanisms such as the India-Central Asia Summit.

s: IMBEX is a joint exercise conducted regularly between Armies of India and
x: IMBEX (India-Myanmar Bilateral Exercise) is the regular army exercise between India and Myanmar; the notes do not cover it.

s:
Consider the following statements about the India’s Look East Policy.

I. It was articulated during the reign of HD Deve Gowda as India’s Prime Minister.

II. It is directed towards South Asian Region.

III. It is about controlling terrorism.

IV. It seeks to develop a bond among various countries on the basis of economic cooperation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
As what kind of policy was the Act East Policy initially conceived?
x: Act East began as an economic policy and was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields with an Indo-Pacific orientation.

s: Countering China's influence, access to new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were drivers of which policy of India?
x: Countering China, new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were the drivers of the Look East Policy (1991-92).

s: Which is the fourth C added to the Commerce, Culture and Connectivity framework of the Act East Policy?
x: The 4th C is Capacity building, not Climate action.

s: With which country is the Akhaura-Agartala railway link associated?
x: Akhaura-Agartala is a rail link with Bangladesh, not an ASEAN-linked project like Kaladan and the Trilateral Highway.

s: Under the Act East Policy, which region of India is the gateway to ASEAN?
x: The North-East is India's gateway to ASEAN under Act East.

s: In which year did India and Vietnam raise their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
x: Under Act East, India-Vietnam ties became a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2016.

s: Which ASEAN country became India's strategic partner in August 2025?
x: India and the Philippines became strategic partners in August 2025; Malaysia's ties became a CSP in 2024.

s: Which of the following countries has passed a resolution to maintain forest on 70% land of its geographical area?
x: Bhutan has constitutionally committed to keep at least 60% of its land under forest cover; the notes do not cover this.

s: What did the Gujral Doctrine, one of the roots of Neighbourhood First, emphasise?
x: The Gujral Doctrine emphasised non-reciprocity, non-interference and not allowing a country's territory to be used against a neighbour.

s: The leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in in May 2014, marking the launch of Neighbourhood First?
x: SAARC leaders were invited to the May 2014 swearing-in; BIMSTEC leaders were invited in 2019.

s: In 2019, the leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in, extending Neighbourhood First?
x: SAARC leaders were invited in May 2014; BIMSTEC leaders in 2019.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: Dustlik-2019 - a first ever joint military exercise was held between India and ___:
What is the importance of developing Chabahar Port by India?
o: India's trade with African countries will enormously increase.
India's relations with oil-producing Arab countries will be strengthened.
India will not depend on Pakistan for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
Pakistan will facilitate and protect the installation of a gas pipeline between Iraq and India.
x: Chabahar Port will provide India with an alternative trade route to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan, which denies India land access to these regions

s: In 2026, what did the USA do with India's sanctions waiver for Chabahar port?
x: In 2026 the USA ended, not extended, India's Chabahar waiver; Chabahar gives India access to Afghanistan, Central Asia and the INSTC bypassing Pakistan.

s: What bilateral trade target was set when India-Uzbekistan ties were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2026?
x: The August 2026 upgrade set a $5 billion trade target by 2030, along with a uranium-supply framework.

s: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers was hosted by which country and held at which city?
x: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019. Afghanistan was also invited.

s: When and how was the first India-Central Asia Summit held?
x: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held virtually in January 2022.

s: On which water body is Iran's Chabahar port located?
x: Chabahar is on the Gulf of Oman and gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia avoiding Pakistan.

s: Besides the Central Asian states, which country was invited to the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019?
x: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers (Samarkand, 2019) also invited Afghanistan.

s: Besides India, Israel and the USA, which country is a member of the I2U2, called the 'West Asia Quad'?
x: I2U2 is India, Israel, UAE and USA.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's Link West engagement:
1. India's trade with the GCC is over $160 billion.
2. The first I2U2 leaders' summit was held virtually in 2022.
3. I2U2 is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: GCC trade exceeds $160 billion, the first I2U2 summit was virtual (2022) and it is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.

s: Which grouping is India's largest socio-economic partner in West Asia, with trade of over $160 billion?
x: The GCC is India's largest socio-economic partner in the region, with over $160 billion trade and about 10 million Indians.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's maritime visions?
o: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region
SAGAR was announced in Sri Lanka in 2015
MAHASAGAR (2025) stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
SHANTI was announced on 13 July 2026 by EAM Jaishankar
x: SAGAR (2015) and MAHASAGAR (2025) were both announced in Mauritius, not Sri Lanka.

s: In which sea area is SHANTI, India's normative framework for shared maritime spaces, to be operationalised first?
x: SHANTI is a normative framework for shared maritime spaces to be operationalised first in the Bay of Bengal.

s: Under the SAGAR doctrine, how does India project itself in the Indian Ocean Region?
o: Junior partner of an external power
x: SAGAR presents India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region, partly in response to China's String of Pearls.

s: In which country was SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) announced in 2015?
x: SAGAR was announced in Mauritius in 2015; MAHASAGAR was also announced in Mauritius (2025).

s: Who launched SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces, on 13 July 2026?
x: SHANTI was launched by EAM Jaishankar, not the PM.

s: In which year was SAGAR upgraded to MAHASAGAR?
x: MAHASAGAR came in 2025 (Mauritius); SAGAR was 2015 and SHANTI 2026.

s: What is the full form of SAGAR in India's maritime policy?
o: Security and Growth for All in the Region
Strategic Alliance for Growth and Regional Security
Security and Governance in the Asian Region
Shared Advancement for Growth in the Region
x: SAGAR, announced in Mauritius in 2015, stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region.

s: What is the full form of MAHASAGAR, India's upgraded maritime vision of 2025?
o: Maritime Alliance for Harmony and Security Across Global and Asian Regions
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
Multilateral Holistic Approach to Security and Growth in the Asian Region
Mutual Help and Security Agreement for Growth and Regional Advancement
x: MAHASAGAR, announced in Mauritius in 2025, means Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.

s: What is the full form of SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces announced in July 2026?
o: Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity
Security and Harmony Among Nations Through Integration
Shared Harbours and Navigation Through Indian Ocean
Strategic Harmony and Norms for Trade in the Indo-Pacific
x: SHANTI, announced by EAM Jaishankar on 13 July 2026, stands for Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity.

With reference to the 'Trans-Pacific Partnership', consider the following statements:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Where was the 14th East Asia Summit of November 2019, at which PM Modi proposed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, held?
x: IPOI was proposed at the 14th EAS in Bangkok; it is an open, non-treaty initiative with seven pillars that builds on SAGAR.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?

s: When did PM Modi set out India's free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific vision at the Shangri-La Dialogue?

s: Which body organises the Shangri-La Dialogue, held in Singapore since 2002?
x: The Shangri-La Dialogue is run by the London-based IISS and has been held in Singapore since 2002.

s: How many pillars does the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) have?
x: IPOI has seven pillars, from Maritime Security to Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport.

s:
Consider the following statements with respect to Information Fusion Centre (IFC) for the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and choose the correct code given below:
a. It is established with a prime vision to strengthen maritime security in the region and beyond
b. Its prime goal is to create maritime information hub for joint satellite mission in the region
c. It has been established at Gurugram, India and is jointly administered by the Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: According to the A.P. Reorganization Act of 2014, Which of the following is the deadline for the division of assets and liabilities between A.P. and Telangana
‘Pivot to Asia’ is the strategy of the foreign policy of
x: Pivot to Asia’ is the strategy of the foreign policy of the United States of America (U.S.A.).

s: Larry Pressler is associated with -
o: Ending of U.S. sanctions on military assistance to
To strengthen cordial relations between U.S and
Criticizing the proposed Military help to Pakistan by
Announcement of candidate for Presidential elections
x: Larry Pressler was a U.S Senator who brought up the Pressler Amendment in 1986, to link US assistance with nuclear non-proliferation. He criticized the US assistance to Pakistan by the Clinton administration on the grounds of Pakistan’s involvement in nuclear proliferation.

s: Which development is regarded as the turning point in India-US relations?
x: The 2008 India-US civil nuclear deal is regarded as the turning point in the relationship.

s: The 'Pivot to Asia' or 'Rebalance' policy of the United States, associated with the Obama era, was announced in which year?
x: The Pivot to Asia, also called the Rebalance, was announced in 2011 during the Obama era to shift greater US strategic attention towards the Asia-Pacific region.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Pressler Amendment?
o: It barred US aid to India over its nuclear programme
It required the US President to certify that Pakistan had no nuclear device
x: The Pressler Amendment barred US aid to Pakistan, not India, unless the President certified Pakistan had no nuclear device; it was applied in 1990.

s: CAATSA (2017) of the USA mainly imposes sanctions on countries that do which of the following?
x: CAATSA provides for US sanctions against buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over its S-400 purchase.

s: How are India-US relations officially described?
x: India-US ties are described as a Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.

s: India sought a CAATSA waiver from the US over its purchase of which Russian system?
x: CAATSA (2017) sanctions buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over the S-400.

s: Kovvada, the proposed site for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kovvada is in Srikakulam district and is the proposed site for the Westinghouse AP1000 reactors under India-US nuclear cooperation.

s: In which year was the Hyde Act, which made the India-US civil nuclear deal possible under US law, passed?
x: The Hyde Act of 2006 came before the 123 Agreement of 2008.

s: When did the NSG grant India the clean waiver that allowed civil nuclear trade?
x: The Nuclear Suppliers Group gave India a clean waiver in September 2008.

s:
Arrange the steps of the India-US civil nuclear deal in chronological order:
1. 123 Agreement
2. Hyde Act
3. NSG clean waiver
x: Hyde Act (2006), then the 123 Agreement (2008), then the NSG clean waiver (September 2008).

s: Which agreement of 2008 is the India-US civil nuclear cooperation agreement?
x: The 123 Agreement of 2008 is the civil nuclear cooperation agreement; the Hyde Act of 2006 is the US law that made it possible.

s: Which reactors are proposed at Kovvada in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh under India-US civil nuclear cooperation?
x: Kovvada (Srikakulam) is the proposed site for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors.

s: In which year was LEMOA, an India-US foundational defence agreement, signed?
x: GSOMIA was signed in 2002, LEMOA in 2016, COMCASA in 2018 and BECA in 2020.

s: What does the STA-1 status, granted by the US to India in 2018, give India?
o: Licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology
Access only to civilian nuclear technology
A veto over US defence exports to third countries
x: STA-1 allows faster, licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology, comparable to NATO allies, without NATO membership.

s:
Consider the following statements about India–US foundational agreements:
1. GSOMIA concerns the protection of shared military information.
2. BECA concerns encrypted communications data and equipment.
3. COMCASA concerns encrypted communications data and equipment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: GSOMIA protects shared military information and COMCASA covers encrypted communications; BECA (2020) concerns geospatial data, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: In which year did the United States designate India as a 'Major Defense Partner'?
x: The United States designated India as a Major Defense Partner in 2016.

s: What does BECA (2020), an India-US foundational agreement, deal with?
o: Geospatial data for navigation and missile targeting
x: BECA covers geospatial (satellite) data; encrypted communications is COMCASA, refuelling is LEMOA and military information is GSOMIA.

s: Which India–US foundational agreement was the first to be signed, in 2002?
x: The order is GSOMIA 2002, LEMOA 2016, COMCASA 2018 and BECA 2020.

s: Which pair of India-US defence milestones both date from 2018?
x: COMCASA and STA-1 status both came in 2018; LEMOA and Major Defense Partner are 2016.

s: Who signed the 10-year India-US defence framework of October 2025 on behalf of India?
x: The 10-year defence framework of October 2025 was signed by US Defence Secretary Hegseth and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.

s: With which company are GE F414 jet engines to be co-produced in India?
x: GE F414 engines are to be co-produced with HAL, not BEL; iCET (2023) was relaunched as TRUST in 2025.

s: What is the outlay of the India Semiconductor Mission launched in December 2021?
x: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in December 2021 with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.

s: India became which signatory of the Artemis Accords in June 2023?
x: India signed the Artemis Accords in June 2023 as the 27th signatory.

s: Under what name was the India-US Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET) relaunched in 2025?
x: iCET (2023) was relaunched as TRUST in February 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India-US technology cooperation?
o: GE F414 jet engines are to be co-produced with BEL
TRUST added critical minerals such as lithium and rare earths
TRUST added biotechnology to semiconductors, AI and quantum
x: GE F414 engines are to be co-produced with HAL, not BEL.

o: joint military exercise between India and USA

joint tiger conservation exercise between India and USA
joint tiger conservation exercise between India and Japan

s: U.S.A. and Indian forces carried out a joint 'Yudha Abhyas' in October 2009. In which State of India it was carried out?
x: Indo-US Joint Exercise Yudh Abhyas-IX was conducted at Babin, India from 12-29 October, 2009. Yudh Abhyas exercise was conducted in Uttarakhand in November 2022. 21st Edition of Yudh Abhyas was conducted from 1st to 14th September, 2025 in USA.

s: In which area was the Indo-US military exercise 'Yudh Abhyas 2014' held ?
x: Indo-US joint military training exercise was conducted from 17th September to 30th September 2014. The practice started on 17th September 2014 in Ranikhet (Uttarakhand) and Chaubatia. This was the 10th exercise of the War Exercise Series, which was started in the year 2004 under the 'Pacific Partnership Program' of the US Army. 20th Edition of Yudh Abhyas was conducted from 9th to 22nd September 2024 in Mahjan Field Firing Ranges, Rajasthan. 21st edition of Yudh Abhyas was conducted from 1 to 14 September, 2025 at fort Wainwright and the Yukon Training Area in Alaska, USA.

s: ‘Red Flag’ is the name of a joint exercise between India and which one of the following countries?
x: Red Flag is a multinational air exercise hosted by the US Air Force, so the partner country is the USA.

s: Which of the following statements is correct with regard to Yudh Abhyas?
o: It is an Indian military exercise with regard to Pakistan.
It is an Indian military exercise with Oman.
It is an Indian military exercise with Bhutan.
It is an Indian military exercise with the US.
x: Yudh Abhyas is the Indo-US Army exercise, so option 4 is correct; it is not held with Pakistan, Oman or Bhutan.

s: What was the code name given to the first ever tri-service military exercise between India and USA?
x: Tiger Triumph is the India-US tri-service amphibious exercise, so the code name is Tiger Triumph.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Vajra Prahar involves Special Forces; Yudh Abhyas is Army, Cope India is Air Force and Tiger Triumph is tri-service amphibious.

s:
Consider the following statements about India–US military exercises:
1. Yudh Abhyas is a naval exercise.
2. Tiger Triumph is a tri-service amphibious exercise.
3. Red Flag is a US Air Force multinational exercise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Tiger Triumph is tri-service and amphibious and Red Flag is a US Air Force multinational exercise; Yudh Abhyas is an Army exercise, so statement 1 is wrong.

s: Cope India is an India-US exercise of which service?
x: Cope India is the Air Force exercise; Malabar is naval and Yudh Abhyas is Army.

s: Vajra Prahar between India and the US is an exercise of which force?
x: Vajra Prahar is a Special Forces exercise; Yudh Abhyas is the Army exercise.

s: Malabar is a naval exercise of India and the USA held along with which other countries?
x: Malabar is a naval exercise of India and the USA with Japan and Australia.

s: In which State was the India-US army exercise Yudh Abhyas held in November 2022?
x: Yudh Abhyas of November 2022 was held in Uttarakhand.

src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officer, Town Planning

s:

s: Who was the first Indian American elected to the US Congress, in 1956?
x: Dalip Singh Saund won a House seat from California in 1956, the first Indian American (and first Asian American) in Congress.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

x: Hage Geingob was re-elected President of Namibia in November 2019. (He died in February 2024; Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah has been President since March 2025.) (Moved to the foreign relations row.)

s: What kind of partnership do India and Japan share?

s: Which U.N. Secretary General served for the longest period?

s: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations?
x: Trygve Lie took office in 1946, followed by Hammarskjold (1953), U Thant (1961) and Waldheim (1972).

s: Who was the first African Secretary-General of the United Nations?
x: Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt was the first African SG; Kofi Annan came after him. U Thant was the first Asian SG.

s: Who was the first Asian Secretary-General of the United Nations?
x: U Thant of Burma (1961-71) was the first Asian Secretary-General.

s: To which country does the present UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres belong?

s: Who was the first Latin American Secretary-General of the United Nations?

s: Dag Hammarskjold, the second Secretary-General of the UN, belonged to which country?
x: Dag Hammarskjold (1953-61) was from Sweden; Trygve Lie, the first, was from Norway.

x: T.S. Tirumurti served as the Permanent Representative from May 2020 to June 2022. As of January 2026, the Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations in New York is Parvathaneni Harish. He assumed office on September 1, 2024, succeeding Ruchira Kamboj.

s: Who among the following has been the first person to deliver his speech in Hindi at U.N.O.?
x: Atal Bihari Vajpayee is the first Indian to deliver a speech in Hindi at the United Nations Assembly. He delivered the speech on 4 October, 1977 as Foreign Minister. During the 69th opening ceremony of the United Nations on 27th September, 2014, Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered his speech in Hindi. By doing this, he became the second Prime Minister, and third Indian leader to do so. It is noteworthy that in the Year 1988, P.V. Narashima Rao (the then Foreign Minister) addressed the United Nations session in Hindi.

x: Ruchira Kamboj served as India's permanent representative to the United Nations from August 2022 to May 2024. She was the first woman to become India's ambassador to the United Nations. x: Dalveer Bhandari was elected as a Judge in the International Court of Justice, on 27th April, 2012 on behalf of India. He was re-elected from 6th February, 2018 for a term of nine years.

s: Which Indian has been elected as a Judge of the International Court of Justice in 2012?
x: Justice Dalveer Bhandari has been elected a judge of the International Court of Justice. He will remain in this post for only 6 years till February, 2018 (normally the judge’s term in the International Court of Justice is for 9 years) but he has to complete the remaining term of Jordan Judge, Awn Shawakat Al-Khasawneh. He is the fourth Indian Judge (after Sir Benegal Rao, Dr. Nagendra Singh and R.S. Pathak) to reach this position. In November, 2017. Justice Dalveer Bhandari was elected as a judge of the International Court of Justice for a second term.
